title: Follow one RPC through its failure-sensitive boundaries
description: Switch scenarios to see which HTTP/2 path is active, where the contract changes, and what the caller can safely conclude.

nodes.label: Native gRPC client
nodes.detail: Creates one call deadline, sends request metadata, consumes responses, and cancels work that is no longer useful.

nodes.label: Resolver + channel policy
nodes.detail: Resolves eligible addresses, maintains subchannels, and picks a ready HTTP/2 connection according to the configured policy.

nodes.label: Backend A
nodes.detail: Checks authorization and remaining deadline, runs the method, propagates context, and returns one final gRPC status.

nodes.label: Backend B
nodes.detail: Can receive a later eligible retry when the first attempt ends with a configured retryable status.

nodes.label: Downstream dependency
nodes.detail: Receives only the remaining deadline and cancellation context, not a newly reset timeout.

nodes.label: Bounded stream buffer
nodes.detail: Separates server production from client consumption with an explicit queue limit and cancellation policy.

scenarios.label: Unary success
scenarios.summary: A bounded lookup reaches Backend A and its dependency before the deadline.
scenarios.result: The server returns a response and OK status. The client can use the result because it arrived inside the same call deadline.

scenarios.label: Deadline propagation
scenarios.summary: The downstream query is still running when the caller's original deadline expires.
scenarios.result: The client observes DEADLINE_EXCEEDED. Cancellation propagates through Backend A; both services must stop application work. Earlier side effects are not rolled back.

scenarios.label: Safe UNAVAILABLE retry
scenarios.summary: A read-only attempt reaches Backend A, which becomes unavailable before returning response headers.
scenarios.result: The configured policy waits its bounded backoff and picks Backend B. The retry remains inside the original deadline and is safe because the operation has no duplicate effect.

scenarios.label: Slow stream consumer
scenarios.summary: Backend A produces server-stream messages faster than the client application processes them.
scenarios.result: HTTP/2 flow control limits transport data in flight, but the application still needs a bounded queue. Slow or abandoned consumers must pause production, shed optional messages, or cancel the stream before memory grows without bound.
